title: Russian Hackers Wait for Victims to Reply Before Sending the Real Malware
content_md: Russian state threat actor Star Blizzard is using email conversations to deliver malware after victims respond to seemingly harmless messages. Microsoft Threat Intelligence detailed the activity in a September 29, 2026, report, describing a delivery technique called RedFlick that supports installation of the CosmicPulse backdoor. Microsoft observed at least 13 large phishing campaigns between January and August 2026. The activity affected more than 100 organizations, primarily in the United States and United Kingdom. Targets included government agencies, think tanks, financial institutions, and organizations supporting Ukraine. The campaigns mark a shift from carefully selected spear-phishing targets toward broader outreach. Attackers send invitations to policy discussions, conferences, and private meetings, using familiar names and organizations to encourage recipients to reply. Russian Hackers Await Replies Once a recipient responds, the attackers typically send a password-protected RAR or ZIP archive. They provide the password as an image inside the email. The attachment contains files that begin the RedFlick infection process. This approach separates the initial contact from malware delivery. The opening message usually contains no attachment, while the later archive arrives within an established conversation.
